newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end with pared losses on fund buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end with pared losses on fund buying.

text.p: Thai stocks closed with pared losses on Friday, after sliding over 3.0 percent late on more foreign sales, as mutual funds bought and on technical support for the index at the 805-level, brokers said.
The SET Index which hit a day-low of 804.49 points at one point finished at 816.79, down 15.81 points or 1.90 percent. The SET 50 at 61.00, down 1.55 points on trade worth 5.54 billion baht.
"I think the market just has no positive news, I think the foreigners were still the main sellers," said Somchai Traitrattanapirom, vice-president at Sitca Investment and Securities.
The index closing level today was the lowest in 51 months. On September 16, 1992, the index finished at 813.33.
"There was some buying from the mutual funds toward the end," said a trader at Nava Finance and Securities.
The mutual funds were believed by brokers to be acting for a private 15 billion baht fund set up by brokers and banks in September and which has entered the market intermittently.

News the Bank of Thailand had called a news conference, just before the market closed, to help allay fears about market talk that Thai banks were hit hard by non-performing loan to the property sector lent support, brokers said.

Later, the central bank said non-performing loans of Thai banks were not as bad as in Malaysia or Indonesia. Thai banks non-performing loans at end-June, excluding that of the ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce, were 7.73 percent of outstanding loans. The market was throughout the day hit by continued sales of blue chips by foreigners.
Foreigners have been net sellers of the Thai market since June and are likely to remain so in the short term.
The kingdom's leading commercial banks topped the active list. Thai Farmers Bank lost four to 124, Krung Thai Bank fell 3.25 to 48.75 and Bangkok Bank gained one baht to 195.
